panels.title: Orphan-Version Backlog
panels.description: Live count of orphaned object versions waiting for the orphan-version reaper. Steady non-zero under churn is normal; sustained growth means the reaper cannot keep up (check reap_errors and reaper activity below).

panels.title: Oldest Orphan Version Age
panels.description: Age of the oldest unreaped orphan version. Growing unbounded = a version the reaper cannot process (writer marker stuck, live head guard, or a reap error) — space and index entries for it are not being reclaimed.

panels.title: Orphan Reap Errors (cumulative, must be 0)
panels.description: Cumulative errors while reaping orphan versions. Any non-zero value means garbage is accumulating: find the failing version in KMS logs. Alert candidate.

panels.title: Commits Rejected: Version Reclaimed (cumulative, must be 0)
panels.description: KMS-side fence: a client tried to commit a version the reaper had already reclaimed. Non-zero = a slow/zombie writer raced the reaper — data is safe (the commit was refused) but the client saw a failed write. Alert candidate.

panels.title: KST Committed-Slot Write Rejections (cumulative, must be 0)
panels.description: KST-side fence backstop: a fragment write arrived for a slot already committed/reclaimed. Non-zero = the fence triangle caught a late writer at the media edge — investigate with the reclaim & commit fences row below. Alert candidate.

panels.title: Reclaim Fences Cleared (cumulative)
panels.description: Cumulative reclaim fences cleared by KMS after orphan reclamation completed. This should tick along with reaper activity; a large gap between versions reaped and fences cleared means fences are being left behind.

panels.title: Write-lease reaping (per second)
panels.description: Rate of write leases reaped by the current-era sweeper vs the legacy expired-write-intent counter (legacy window path only). Sustained lease reaping means clients are dying mid-write or failing to renew — cross-check renew/forfeit RPC rates to the right.

panels.title: Lease-control RPCs (per second)
panels.description: Renew and forfeit RPC rates from clients. renew_write_lease should track long-running writes; forfeit_object_write is a client abandoning a write cleanly — a forfeit spike alongside lease reaping points at client-side failures.

panels.title: Write Leases Reaped (cumulative)
panels.description: Cumulative write leases reaped since KMS start. Zero on a healthy cluster with well-behaved clients; every increment is one writer that vanished without forfeiting.

panels.title: Backlog over time
panels.description: Orphan-version backlog per KMS instance. This is background debt: a sawtooth is healthy (accumulate → reap); a monotonic climb means the reaper is stuck or outpaced. NOT the same mechanism as legacy orphan GC (next row).

panels.title: Oldest orphan age over time
panels.description: Age of the oldest unreaped orphan version per KMS instance. A flat plateau that keeps rising linearly = one specific version is unreapable (check skipped_head_live / skipped_writer_alive and reap_errors).

panels.title: Reap errors (per second, must stay 0)
panels.description: Rate of orphan-version reap failures. Any blip here is a bug or an FDB availability issue; the affected versions stay in the backlog and pin the oldest-age gauge.

panels.title: Reaper activity (per second)
panels.description: Scan → claim → reap pipeline rates plus resumed reaps after interruption. Claimed should roughly equal reaped; a persistent gap means reaps are being abandoned mid-flight (look at resumed and reap errors).

panels.title: Reaper skips (per second)
panels.description: Versions the reaper deliberately left alone: head became live again, the writer's lease is still alive, or a tombstone already covers it. Skips are safety behavior, not errors — but a version stuck in skipped_writer_alive forever means a lease that never expires.

panels.title: Cleanup detail (per second)
panels.description: What each reap actually deleted: metadata rows cleared, KCO1 index entries cleared, and storage targets cleaned of fragments. Targets-cleaned lagging rows-cleared means target-side deletion is falling behind metadata deletion.

panels.title: Legacy orphan GC (separate mechanism — not the orphan-version reaper)
Legacy orphan GC activity (per second)
panels.description: The OLDER, separate orphan mechanism (orphan_gc_*): sweeps allocation orphans from the legacy window path, distinct from the orphan-version reaper above. If the legacy write path carries no traffic these should be flat at 0; activity here means legacy-path writes are still happening.

panels.title: Legacy orphan GC — lease-active skips (per second)
panels.description: Legacy-GC candidates skipped because a write lease was still active. Persistent activity means legacy-path writers are long-lived enough to collide with the GC interval.

panels.title: Legacy GC Freed (cumulative)
panels.description: Cumulative allocations freed by the legacy orphan GC since KMS start. On a cluster running only the current write path this stays frozen — movement means legacy traffic exists.

panels.title: Fence triangle (per second)
panels.description: The three fence signals together: fences cleared (normal reclaim completion), KMS commits rejected because the version was reclaimed, and KST writes rejected against committed slots. Cleared ticking with reaper activity is healthy; ANY rejection is a caught race and warrants investigation even though data stayed safe.

panels.title: Committed-slot write rejections per target
panels.description: KST fence backstop broken out per target (cumulative counter shown raw so a single historical rejection stays visible). One target accumulating rejections points at a client repeatedly retrying stale fragments toward that drive.

panels.title: Commit RPC rate by flavor (per second)
panels.description: All commit flavors — single-shot commit_object, streamed commit_object_segmented, and batched multi_commit_object — split by RPC. Context for the fence panels: rejections should be vanishingly rare relative to this commit volume.

panels.title: Write-profile routing decisions (per second)
panels.description: BeginObject storage-class routing: every write passes write_profile_class_route; write_profile_alternate counts small objects rerouted to a bucket's replicated profile, write_profile_default counts writes kept on the bucket's default EC profile. alternate/route ratio = fraction of small-object traffic.

panels.title: Routing decision latency (µs) — pow2-bucketed approx
panels.description: Latency of the write_profile_class_route phase inside BeginObject. Should be near-zero (a cached catalog lookup); growth means the EC-profile catalog cache is thrashing. Note: p99 is a power-of-2 bucketed approximation; avg is exact.

panels.title: EC-Profile Catalog Cache Hit %
panels.description: Hit ratio of the EC-profile catalog cache feeding profile selection and class routing (from begin_object phase sample counters). Should sit near 100% in steady state; misses mean FDB round-trips on the write hot path.

panels.title: Not yet instrumented: FDB transaction health
panels.description: Placeholder for the FoundationDB transaction-health row. Nothing to render until KMS instruments its FDB client.

options.content:
**Missing instrumentation (gap C6).** The KMS stat tree exposes **no FoundationDB metrics at all** — no txn commit latency, no conflict/retry counts, no transaction-too-old counters — despite the multi-threaded FDB client (commit 61ba0a1). Until KMS instruments the FDB layer and keinexport exports it, FDB stalls will only show up indirectly as inflated `store_*` phase latencies on the KMS Detail dashboard.

Planned panels for this row once C6 lands: FDB commit latency (avg/p99/max), conflict-retry rate, txn-too-old rate, per-shard txn volume.

panels.title: Net granules by storage class
panels.description: Physical slots (granules) attributable to each storage class: committed minus deleted, counted by KMS at commit/delete time. These are counters since KMS process start — a restart resets them to zero, so read per-class growth rate and mix, not absolute level; KST granule occupancy (Fleet Overview → Capacity) is the absolute truth for physical fill.

panels.title: Net logical bytes by storage class
panels.description: Logical object bytes attributable to each storage class: committed minus deleted. Same caveat as the granule panel: counters since KMS process start (restarts reset to zero) — use this for per-class growth and traffic mix, and KST occupancy for absolute physical truth.

panels.title: Physical amplification by class (x)
panels.description: Physical bytes consumed per logical byte stored, by class: net granules × average extent size ÷ net logical bytes. Expect rep-1-2 to cost ~3x at extent-filling object sizes and worse below (a tiny object still burns whole granules on 3 targets); shrunk-EC costs ~10 granules per ≤ 1 MiB object. A class drifting upward means its object-size mix is getting smaller/less efficient — reconsider its routing threshold or profile.

targets.expr: (sum by (class) (keinfs_kms_class_committed_granules_total) - sum by (class) (keinfs_kms_class_deleted_granules_total)) * scalar(avg(keinfs_kst_extent_bytes)) / clamp_min(sum by (class) (keinfs_kms_class_committed_logical_bytes_total) - sum by (class) (keinfs_kms_class_deleted_logical_bytes_total), 1)

panels.title: Commit rate by class (obj/s)
panels.description: Objects committed per second per storage class (5m rate). Shows where write traffic is landing after storage-class routing — small-object traffic should appear under the replicated class if routing is working. A class stuck at 0 while its buckets take writes means routing never selects it; compare with the routing-decision panel above.

panels.title: Inventory & placement RPCs (per second)
panels.description: Target registration, heartbeats, inventory listing, admin state changes, and computed-placement reservations. heartbeat_target should be a steady floor of targets × heartbeat rate; a drop = targets falling out of the inventory. reserve_computed_placement tracks decentralized-placement write setup.

panels.title: Target failure / lifecycle RPCs (per second)
panels.description: Failure reports and drain/recover/retire admin actions. Anything non-zero here is an operator action or a client reporting a bad target — correlate with rebuild activity and per-target error counters on the KST overview.

panels.title: Repair writes (per second)
panels.description: repair_object_write is the degraded-write path: a client repairing fragments after a failed target. Should be 0 in steady state; sustained activity means clients keep hitting bad targets — check which targets in the failure-RPC panel.

panels.title: Repair phase latency (µs) — pow2-bucketed approx
panels.description: Where repair-write time goes inside KMS: replacement-placement reservation vs the store write. Note: p99 is a power-of-2 bucketed approximation; avg is exact.

panels.title: Heartbeat / placement RPC latency (µs) — pow2-bucketed approx
panels.description: Latency of heartbeat_target and reserve_computed_placement. Heartbeats are the target-liveness heartbeat of the whole inventory: rising latency here predicts spurious target-down decisions. Note: p99 is a power-of-2 bucketed approximation; avg is exact.

panels.title: Sweeper runs (per second)
panels.description: Background sweeper execution rate per KMS instance. Should be a steady cadence at the configured interval; gaps mean the sweeper is stuck (and lease reaping / orphan scanning stop with it).

panels.title: Sweeper run latency (µs, avg)
panels.description: Average wall time of one sweeper run and of its release work. A run time approaching the sweep interval means the sweeper saturates and background debt (backlog, unreaped leases) starts growing.

panels.title: Sweeper Runs (cumulative)
panels.description: Cumulative background sweeper runs since KMS start. Frozen value while the process is up = the sweeper task died.

panels.title: Not yet instrumented: KRS rebuild daemon
panels.description: Placeholder for the rebuild row. The rebuild story is dark until keinexport gains keinfs_krs_* families.

options.content:
**Missing export (gap C2).** keinexport exports **zero `keinfs_krs_*` families**, so the rebuild daemon (leased tasks, active task, failed tasks, rebuilt bytes) has no dashboard presence. Rebuild progress after a drive failure is currently only observable via the KRS stat tree on disk and indirectly via KMS `repair_object_write` / target-failure RPC rates above.

Planned panels once C2 lands: leased vs completed rebuild tasks, active task gauge, failed tasks (must-be-0), rebuilt bytes/s per target.
